messages:
incident-bot: :bell: ALERT: embedding-service-east experiencing increased p99 latency and connection resets to cache backend (redis-primary-east). Paging @alex. Auto-bridge created: https://zoom.example/bridges/xyz789

alex (oncall): on it, joining bridge. grabbing blast radius and runbooks.

tina (infra): I'm seeing Redis master report failover at 10:16:03 UTC, followed by a burst of reconnects from embedding workers. Metrics: redis.commands rejected spiked.

rory (sre): embedding-worker logs show `ERR_EMPTY_RESPONSE` and client timeouts while waiting on cache GETs. Workers then backpressured requests to downstream model pool.

liz (cust-succ): any idea which customers saw impact? I have a CX ping from a customer reporting slow embeddings in EU.

alex (oncall): initial numbers: global p99 for embeddings rose from 420ms -> 2.1s between 10:15-10:25 UTC. Approx 0.6% of embedding requests timed out. Tagging dedicated caches list now.

tina (infra): Redis provider indicates scheduled maintenance rollback in the region started at 10:12, failed over primary, then replica promotion flapped twice due to networking blips. We're opening a support case.

rory (sre): mitigation plan: 1) divert embedding read traffic for east -> fallback cache cluster (cache-read-failover), 2) increase embedding-worker timeouts and switch to origin on cache failures, 3) restart a subset of workers to re-establish healthy connections. I'll run steps 1+2.

ops-bot: failover read-route update applied: `route update embedding-service --cache-read-fallback cache-read-failover` (took 18s).

alex (oncall): after failover, p99 improved to ~550ms within 3 minutes; error counts dropping. Keeping bridge open for 30m observation.

liz (cust-succ): which customers had dedicated cache? cust-G, cust-H in eu-west. I've started using the incident template to draft outreach.

sana (product-ops): drafting status page blurb: "We experienced a Redis master failover in east that briefly increased embedding latency for a subset of customers. We diverted reads to a fallback cache and recovered service by 10:28 UTC. A post-incident review is scheduled." Will post draft to doc link.

megan (legal): flag: if any SLAs impacted for dedicated caches please call it out. I'll standby for the metrics.

rory (sre): action checklist (quick):
- implement read failover automation for Redis flaps (owner: rory)
- add synthetic embedding probe hitting cache+origin to detect cache degradation (owner: tina)
- improve logging for cache fallback events (owner: rory)
- run postmortem & generate RCA (owner: alex)
- customer outreach templates (owner: liz)

alex (oncall): proposing postmortem at 15:00 UTC tomorrow (60m). Agenda: timeline, root cause (provider maintenance + network flapping), remediation options, customer comms, SLA check. Pre-read in docs: https://docs.redwood/incidents/1720600000-pre-read

rory (sre): I'll attach logs and a small reproducer that simulates rapid replica promotions and connection churn. Reproducer command:```./tools/sim_redis_failover.sh --region east --clients 100 --rate 50``` (internal).

tina (infra): I'll collect provider support case ID and network traceroutes (due: 2026-03-16 12:00 UTC). Also adding long-term: cross-region async replication + automatic reader promotion policy.

liz (cust-succ): I've sent initial status hold messages to cust-G and cust-H with ETA for RCA within 72 hours. Asked them to share any request ids/timestamps they saw.

megan (legal): will review outreach drafts before send. If SLA threshold for p99 or timeouts is crossed, we follow standard credit playbook.

alex (oncall): INCIDENT RESOLVED at 10:28 UTC after stabilization and traffic diversion. Moving to post-incident workflow. Opening incident board and tagging tasks `incident/1720600000`.

sana (product-ops): please link customer-facing note and status page copy into the incident board. I'll own the status page update after legal signs off.

rory (sre): temporary mitigations: 1) add quick read-fallback rule to routing, 2) lower embedding-worker connection retry backoff to recover faster. Permanent items in doc.

alex (oncall): Assigning action item owners + due dates in the incident board:
- rory (sre) -> read-failover automation PR + tests (due: 2026-03-23)
- tina (infra) -> synthetic probe + provider support summary (due: 2026-03-17)
- liz (cust-succ) -> customer RCA outreach and logging of replies (due: 2026-03-16 18:00 UTC)
- megan (legal) -> SLA assessment & review comms (due: 2026-03-17 16:00 UTC)
- alex (oncall) -> postmortem doc + timeline (due: 2026-03-16 15:00 UTC)

liz (cust-succ): will propose personalized follow-ups depending on impact; default tone: apologetic, factual, mitigation steps, next steps for RCA.

(End of thread)
